question: Describe the radiographic findings and give your diagnosis.

keyFindings.finding: Loss of normal periapical trabecular pattern

key.diagnosis: Periapical inflammatory lesion; acute apical abscess only if supported by symptoms and examination

expertExplanation: The image shows periapical radiolucency associated with a restored mandibular molar. Distinguishing an abscess from other apical inflammatory lesions requires clinical findings.

findings: Mandibular posterior periapical radiograph displaying a premolar, first molar, and second molar.
Large radiopaque coronal restorations on all three visible teeth, with small radiopaque retentive pins beneath the restorations in the first and second molars.
Absence of root canal filling material in the pulp chambers and root canals of the visible teeth.

Well-defined periapical radiolucencies (marked by red arrows) surrounding the distal root apex and, to a lesser extent, the mesial root apex of the first molar, accompanied by loss of the apical lamina dura.
aiReading.impression: Apical periodontitis (periapical granuloma, cyst, or abscess) associated with the mandibular first molar
aiReading.limitation: The coronal occlusal surfaces are obscured by the radiographic holder, and lack of clinical pulp vitality testing limits differentiation between specific periapical lesion types.

question: Describe the radiographic findings and give your diagnosis.

keyFindings.finding: Triangular radiolucency at the proximal surface
Lesion extending into the tooth structure

expertExplanation: A proximal radiolucency is visible on the bitewing radiograph. Clinical assessment is needed to determine cavitation and treatment.

findings: Bitewing radiograph showing posterior maxillary and mandibular teeth on one side.
Small radiolucency confined to the outer enamel on the mesial surface of the mandibular second premolar, indicated by the arrow labeled D1.
Radiopaque occlusal restoration on the maxillary molar.
Bright radiopaque mesio-occlusal restoration on the mandibular first molar.
Minimal interproximal calculus or bone loss visible within the maxillary crestal region.
aiReading.impression: Incipient interproximal enamel caries (D1 lesion) on the mesial surface of the mandibular second premolar, with existing posterior restorations.
aiReading.limitation: Cropped field of view excludes the tooth apices and most of the mandibular alveolar bone, and low image resolution limits detection of subtle demineralization.

question: Describe the radiographic findings and give your diagnosis.

keyFindings.finding: Marked loss of supporting alveolar bone
Involvement extending toward the root/apical region

expertExplanation: The radiograph shows extensive destruction of supporting bone adjacent to a compromised tooth. Pulp sensibility and periodontal probing are necessary to classify the lesion.

findings: Two retained root fragments in the central alveolar region with complete loss of the clinical crown
Large, fairly well-defined periapical radiolucency beneath the retained root fragments, extending closely toward the root apex of the adjacent premolar on the right
Mesially inclined molar to the left of the retained roots with a radiopaque occlusal restoration and a large underlying radiolucency approaching the pulp chamber
Mild to moderate alveolar bone loss adjacent to the mesially inclined molar
Superimposed film identification stamp ('ULT') and minor surface artifacts on the rightmost tooth
aiReading.impression: Retained root fragments with associated large periapical radiolucency (consistent with a radicular cyst, periapical granuloma, or abscess) and deep caries in the adjacent tilted molar
aiReading.limitation: Single 2D periapical radiograph without clinical correlation, pulp vitality testing, or full coverage of adjacent teeth limits definitive lesion classification.

question: Describe the radiographic findings and give your diagnosis.

keyFindings.finding: Association with the crown of an unerupted tooth

expertExplanation: The lesion surrounds an unerupted mandibular premolar and displaces it. The published case identifies it as a dentigerous cyst; histopathology is needed for definitive cyst typing.

findings: Well-defined, corticated, unilocular radiolucency in the right mandibular premolar-molar region (outlined by blue arrows)
Unerupted, inferiorly displaced mandibular right second premolar positioned near the lower border of the mandible within the radiolucency (indicated by red arrow)
Thinning of the inferior cortical border of the right mandible subjacent to the lesion
Mild mesial inclination of the mandibular right first molar and abutment of the lesion against adjacent tooth roots
Developing unerupted maxillary and mandibular second molars visible bilaterally
Radiopaque restorations present on the left maxillary and left mandibular posterior teeth
aiReading.impression: Dentigerous cyst associated with an unerupted mandibular right second premolar
aiReading.limitation: Low image resolution, 2D panoramic distortion, and pre-existing overlay arrows limit assessment of subtle root resorption, buccal-lingual expansion, and inferior alveolar canal involvement.

question: Describe the radiographic findings and give your diagnosis.

keyFindings.finding: Ectopic high position relative to the dental arch

expertExplanation: The panoramic radiograph shows an abnormally positioned, unerupted maxillary third molar. Further imaging may be needed when surgical planning requires detailed anatomy.

findings: Impacted and superiorly positioned maxillary right third molar (tooth #1 / FDI 18) overlapping the right maxillary tuberosity and posterior sinus region
Small, well-defined radiopaque occlusal restorations in the mandibular right and left first molars (teeth #30 / FDI 46 and #19 / FDI 36)
Small radiopacity in the crown of the maxillary left first molar (tooth #14 / FDI 26) suggestive of a restoration
Mandibular third molars (teeth #17 / FDI 38 and #32 / FDI 48) and maxillary left third molar (tooth #16 / FDI 28) are not clearly visualized/absent
Grossly intact alveolar bone levels and symmetric mandibular condyles without obvious large periapical radiolucencies
aiReading.impression: Impacted maxillary right third molar (tooth #1 / FDI 18) with minor occlusal restorations in the first molars
aiReading.limitation: Low image resolution, 2D panoramic superimposition, and ghosting/air-space shadows limit assessment of fine caries and exact 3D relationship to the maxillary sinus.

question: Describe the radiographic findings and give your diagnosis.

keyFindings.finding: Multiple unerupted teeth beyond expected positions

expertExplanation: The pretreatment radiographs demonstrate multiple unerupted and displaced teeth. Clinical age and eruption history help distinguish impaction from normal developmental delay.

findings: Mixed dentition with developing permanent dentition and unerupted second molars within bony crypts.
Well-defined cluster of small tooth-like radiopacities in the right mandibular canine-premolar region overlying an inferiorly displaced, impacted permanent tooth.

Horizontally or obliquely positioned tooth-like radiopaque structure in the right anterior maxilla near the nasal floor, with absence of normally erupted right maxillary anterior incisors in the arch.
aiReading.impression: Compound odontoma in the right mandible causing tooth impaction, with concurrent impacted or supernumerary maxillary anterior tooth
aiReading.limitation: Low image resolution, panoramic blur, and cervical spine superimposition in the midline obscure fine root and structural details.

question: Describe the radiographic findings and give your diagnosis.

keyFindings.finding: Location superior to permanent maxillary incisors

expertExplanation: The arrows identify tooth-like radiopaque structures near the roots of maxillary incisors. These are consistent with impacted supernumerary teeth in the published case.

findings: Two well-defined, tooth-like radiopaque structures (indicated by red arrows) superimposed over the roots of both maxillary central incisors.
Left arrow points to a conical, crown-like radiopacity overlapping the mid-to-apical root region of the right maxillary central incisor.
Right arrow points to a second tooth-like radiopacity overlapping the left maxillary central incisor, with a rounded crown-like portion over the mid-root and a root extending superiorly.
Prominent mamelons are visible along the incisal edges of both maxillary central incisors.
The apical regions of the central incisors are partially obscured due to superimposition.
aiReading.impression: Bilateral supernumerary teeth (mesiodentes) in the maxillary anterior region
aiReading.limitation: Single two-dimensional periapical view limits buccal-palatal localization and obscures the underlying central incisor apices without additional angulated views or CBCT.

question: Describe the radiographic findings and give your diagnosis.

keyFindings.finding: Well-defined radiolucent enlargement within the root canal space

expertExplanation: The root canal appears expanded by an intraradicular radiolucency. Angled radiographs or CBCT may help distinguish internal from external resorption.

findings: Well-defined oval radiolucency in the cervical-to-mid-root region of a mandibular incisor (third tooth from the left), obscuring the outline of the root canal space
Periapical radiolucency surrounding the apex of the same affected mandibular incisor with mild apical root blunting
Mild-to-moderate horizontal alveolar bone loss across the mandibular anterior region
Proximal crown overlap and radiopaque restorative material in the premolar region on the right side of the image
aiReading.impression: Internal root resorption with associated periapical radiolucency (external root resorption in the differential diagnosis)
aiReading.limitation: A single two-dimensional periapical radiograph cannot definitively distinguish internal from external root resorption or evaluate buccolingual lesion extent without angled views or CBCT.

question: Describe the radiographic findings and give your diagnosis.

keyFindings.finding: Relatively even bone level across adjacent teeth
Alveolar crest approximately parallel to CEJ line

expertExplanation: The alveolar crest is reduced in height with a broadly horizontal pattern. Clinical periodontal measurements are needed to diagnose and stage periodontitis.

findings: Severe horizontal and vertical alveolar bone loss extending into the apical third of the roots of the mandibular anterior teeth
Loss of lamina dura and ill-defined periapical radiolucency around the central tooth, which appears shortened or coronally displaced
Slight curvature at the root apex of the incisor immediately to the right of the central tooth
Markedly reduced periodontal bone support around all visible anterior roots
aiReading.impression: Severe periodontitis with advanced alveolar bone loss
aiReading.limitation: Low-resolution grainy image and cropping of the tooth crowns at the superior border limit assessment of coronal structures and subgingival calculus.

question: Describe the radiographic findings and give your diagnosis.

keyFindings.finding: Unequal bone heights around adjacent roots
Oblique rather than horizontal bone-loss pattern

expertExplanation: The radiograph demonstrates an angular defect alongside the tooth root. Probing depth, attachment loss and full-mouth findings are required for periodontal diagnosis.

findings: Maxillary premolar in the center of the image exhibits a pronounced S-shaped root curvature (dilaceration) with the pulp canal following the curved root anatomy.
Adjacent premolar (second tooth from the right) shows a well-defined coronal radiolucency on the occlusal/mesial aspect suggestive of caries, fracture, or a radiolucent restoration.
The two leftmost molar teeth demonstrate marked coronal radiopacity consistent with full-coverage restorations or dense restorative material.
A thin corticated line crosses the apical region of the posterior teeth, consistent with the floor of the maxillary sinus.
aiReading.impression: Root dilaceration (S-shaped curvature) of the maxillary second premolar with suspected coronal caries or defect on the adjacent first premolar
aiReading.limitation: Two-dimensional periapical projection with limited image resolution and no clinical correlation restricts evaluation of buccopalatal root angulation and confirmation of coronal defects.
